text.arabic_uthmani: وَبَرًّۢا بِوَٰلِدَيْهِ وَلَمْ يَكُن جَبَّارًا عَصِيًّۭا

words.gloss_range: opening connector continuing the prior portrait into a new positive attribute
words.prose: {{ar:وَ}} ({{tr:wa}}) opens the ayah as continuation, so the filial quality that follows is not a detached new sentence but another element in the carried portrait from 19:13. It can be heard as coordination or circumstance: the point is that the new positive predicate arrives as an added or accompanying state. Its single-letter proclitic form also makes the ayah begin with connection before any new lexical content appears, preparing the positive-to-negative frame that will run through the verse.

topics.headline: continuing portrait hinge
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the ayah begins by carrying the prior portrait forward before adding the filial trait.
topics.reason: The particle is aligned as a conjunction, and the CRITICAL rows consistently treat it as joining or accompanying the previous characterization rather than opening an isolated sentence.

topics.headline: proclitic opening connection
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the first visible form fuses connection to the first positive predicate.
topics.reason: The surface is a particle written as a proclitic before the next word, so the formal observation is locally coherent.

words.gloss_range: dutiful filial goodness as a predicate quality, specified by the following parent phrase
words.root_gloss_range: righteousness, dutifulness, open land, and related concrete extensions; locally the filial righteousness branch is selected while openness colors the image
words.prose: {{ar:بَرًّۢا}} ({{tr:barran}}) is a predicate quality in the continuing portrait, not a narrated single deed. Its accusative and nominal shape make filial goodness a stable state attached to Yahya, and the following parent phrase selects the familiar dutifulness-to-parents sense. The broader root field of open land and nourishment can color the trait as spacious, sustaining goodness, but local grammar keeps the selected sense relational and filial. Variant vowel evidence keeps a pressure between abstract virtue-name and predicate-state, while the local surface still functions as the carried character predicate. The paired formula returns in 19:32 with a mother-only phrase, so 19:14 is marked as a dual-parent version of the same prophetic certification, and the word also begins the ayah sound thread that later lands in the two negated attributes.

topics.headline: predicate quality in the carried chain
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the word assigns durable character, not merely a performed act.
topics.reason: The form is tagged as a gerund or predicate quality and is syntactically continued from the prior characterization frame.

topics.headline: filial piety selected by complement
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that broad goodness is immediately concretized as duty toward parents.
topics.reason: The following prepositional parent phrase is syntactically forced as the complement, selecting the filial sense from the broader range.

topics.headline: open-land goodness as coloring
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices the positive trait as spacious and sustaining, while still reading filial piety as the local sense.
topics.reason: The physical land and nourishment fields are real root evidence, but the parent complement blocks making them separate local referents.

topics.headline: variant pressure toward abstract quality
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that variant vowel evidence exposes a pressure between abstract virtue-name and predicate state.
topics.reason: Variant readings are useful as contrast, while the local surface remains the transmitted predicate form.

topics.headline: paired filial formula in surah 19
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the dual-parent formula in 19:14 is defined against the mother-only reprise in 19:32.
topics.reason: The inter-ayah rows provide concrete same-surah parallels, and the local dual phrase makes the contrast precise.

topics.headline: boundary handoff and cadence
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices the ayah moving from inward virtue into outward filial goodness before the negative closure begins.
topics.reason: The boundary rows and final cadence rows describe a coherent structural movement within the ayah.

words.gloss_range: preposition binding the quality of filial goodness to the parent phrase
words.prose: {{ar:بِ}} ({{tr:bi}}) gives the positive predicate its route: the goodness is not left abstract, but is directed toward and realized through the parent relation. Its range can suggest direction, accompaniment, or means, yet the local attachment chiefly makes the parents the governed complement of the preceding quality. Because the particle is written as a bound form, and because the recited transition carries the nasal ending of the quality into the bilabial preposition, the link is visible and audible. The same mechanism recurs in 19:32, so the structural difference between the two birth portraits falls on the parent noun, not on the prepositional link.

topics.headline: preposition governing filial endpoint
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that filial goodness has a governed endpoint rather than floating as a detached virtue.
topics.reason: Attachment evidence directly marks the parent phrase as the prepositional complement tied to the positive predicate.

topics.headline: direction and medium together
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the parent relation is both the target and the concrete medium in which goodness appears.
topics.reason: The broader prepositional range is meaningful, but local syntax narrows it to the governed filial relation.

topics.headline: bound link in the paired formula
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that a small bound particle audibly and visibly attaches the quality to its object, and the same link recurs in 19:32.
topics.reason: The surface is a bound preposition, and the inter-ayah row gives a concrete same-surah recurrence.

words.gloss_range: his two parents, governed by the preceding preposition and specified by the possessive suffix
words.root_gloss_range: birth, begetting, parenthood, child, and generated forms; locally selected as the active-parent dual relation
words.prose: {{ar:وَٰلِدَيْهِ}} ({{tr:wālidayhi}}) completes the positive beat by naming the governed endpoint of the goodness: his own two parents. The dual form treats father and mother as one paired object, while the suffix keeps Yahya as the same carried subject from the prior portrait. The active-parent form also makes them origin-agents, not generic elders, so the relation being honored is tied to begetting and birth. That matters inside Surah 19, where the same root threads birth, parenthood, and divine-sonship denial; 19:14 names creaturely parents, while 19:32 shifts the formula to a mother-only phrase and 19:35 denies divine child-taking. Structurally, this concrete dual relation closes the positive beat before the ayah widens into objectless negated vices.

topics.headline: governed dual possession
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the positive virtue lands on Yahya’s own two parents as a single governed relation.
topics.reason: The word is genitive under the preceding preposition, dual, and possessed by a 3ms suffix, all matching the CRITICAL claim.

topics.headline: parents as begetting source-agents
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the noun frames the parents as those who generated him, not merely as broad kin.
topics.reason: The local form is a parent active-participle noun, and dictionary evidence supports the begetting-parent branch.

topics.headline: birth and generation thread in surah 19
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices the parent word as one node in Surah 19’s wider birth and generation vocabulary.
topics.reason: The inter-ayah rows name concrete same-surah links, including 19:15, 19:33, and 19:35.

topics.headline: dual-parent contrast with 19:32
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that Yahya’s dual-parent relation contrasts with the mother-only formula for Isa in 19:32.
topics.reason: The same formula recurs with a different parent noun in 19:32, making the contrast locally grounded.

topics.headline: specific relation before objectless negation
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the ayah narrows goodness to a concrete family relation before denying vices without an object.
topics.reason: The first beat ends with the governed parent phrase, while the following negated adjectives are predicate material without explicit objects.

words.gloss_range: connector launching the negated clause as a joined second beat
words.prose: {{ar:وَ}} ({{tr:wa}}) is the hinge between the completed parent-goodness beat and the negative character clause. It can coordinate the negation as the next item or make it circumstantial alongside the positive description, but in either case the two beats remain joined: Yahya is described as dutiful while the tyrant-rebel profile is excluded. Written onto the negator, the particle makes the second launch arrive as a joined-and-negated unit, matching the ayah’s two audible starts.

topics.headline: hinge between virtue and exclusion
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the negative clause adds to the positive portrait instead of replacing it.
topics.reason: The particle sits before the negated clause and joins it to the completed positive beat.

topics.headline: joined negative launch
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices a second audible launch where connection and negation enter together.
topics.reason: The surface fuses the connector to the following negator, and the prosodic row aligns with the two-beat structure.

words.gloss_range: past negator governing the following jussive copula and scoping over the two predicate traits
words.prose: {{ar:لَمْ}} ({{tr:lam}}) defines the second beat before the verb or adjectives arrive: both following traits fall under one negator. The force is not a bare present absence; it denies that the coercive and disobedient states ever obtained in Yahya’s portrait. The particle has no lexical root-work here, but it visibly controls the shortened verb that follows, making negation and morphology one package. In Surah 19, that matters because the same being-disobedient frame is later affirmed for Satan in 19:44, while here it is categorically barred.

topics.headline: single negator over the vice pair
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that both final traits are excluded by one governing negative operator.
topics.reason: Attachment evidence marks the negated copular construction, and the following predicate and modifier remain within that clause.

topics.headline: state never obtained
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices a character verdict across the portrait, not merely the absence of a trait at one moment.
topics.reason: The particle plus jussive construction supports past-state negation rather than simple present negation or delayed occurrence.

topics.headline: particle control without root semantics
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that a small rootless particle still governs the visible shape and sound of the verb.
topics.reason: The row about an l-m-m root is narrowed as a database-artifact warning; locally the word is a primitive negative particle controlling the jussive.

topics.headline: negated frame before 19:44 contrast
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the frame denied here will later be affirmed for a rebel figure in 19:44.
topics.reason: The row gives a concrete same-surah contrast and does not override the local parse.

words.gloss_range: negated jussive copula carrying Yahya as implicit subject and opening predicate slots for the denied traits
words.root_gloss_range: being, existing, becoming, place or standing extensions; locally a copular being-state under negation
words.prose: {{ar:يَكُنْ}} ({{tr:yakun}}) is not a transitive action verb here; it opens a copular slot where the two final adjectives supply the denied identities. Its 3ms morphology keeps Yahya present without restating his name, while the preceding negator clips the verb into a jussive shape, giving the negative beat a compressed stop before the heavy predicates. The broader root range of being, becoming, and standing supports the positive payoff that Yahya never occupied or entered those character states, though the local frame remains a copular predicate construction. Surah 19 repeatedly uses being-language for character taxonomy: 19:13 affirms piety, 19:14 denies rebellion, 19:44 affirms disobedience for Satan, and 19:51 certifies Musa. The same being-tyrant accusation frame appears in 28:19, but 19:14 turns that possibility into a denied character state.

topics.headline: copular predicate frame
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the ayah denies identity-states, not isolated actions.
topics.reason: Attachment evidence marks the verb as copular with predicate material following, and QAC identifies it as the imperfect jussive of the copula.

topics.headline: implicit Yahya subject
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that morphology carries Yahya into the negative clause without repeating his name.
topics.reason: The verb is 3ms with an implicit subject, matching the carried referent in the portrait.

topics.headline: jussive compression after negation
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the clipped verb shape makes the negated frame feel terse and controlled.
topics.reason: The preceding negator governs the jussive form, and the apocopated shape is visible in the local surface.

topics.headline: being and becoming range
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the negation bars both occupying and entering the named character states.
topics.reason: The k-w-n range includes being and becoming, but local syntax keeps it inside the copular predicate frame rather than activating place or surety branches independently.

topics.headline: surah 19 being taxonomy
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the same being-frame classifies prophetic and rebel characters across Surah 19.
topics.reason: The CRITICAL rows give concrete same-surah references, and the local verb belongs to the same predicate-frame pattern.

topics.headline: being-jabbar accusation contrast
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the clause pivots from a specified parent relation into a universal denial of tyrant identity, echoing accusation language in 28:19.
topics.reason: The row supplies a concrete parallel frame, and the local sequence is the ayah hinge from relation to unrestricted character exclusion.

words.gloss_range: negated intensive predicate meaning an overbearing coercive character type in this human context
words.root_gloss_range: repair, restoration, compulsion, overpowering force, and divine irresistibility; locally narrowed to blameworthy human coercion under negation
words.prose: {{ar:جَبَّارًا}} ({{tr:jabbāran}}) is the first predicate supplied to the negated copula, so the ayah denies a character class rather than one coercive act. The root’s repair-by-force image gives the word its bite: in a human predicate under negation, forced restoration becomes illegitimate domination, not neutral strength. That human vice is distinct from the divine epithet field at 59:23 and matches human accusation or tyrant-group contexts such as 28:19 and 5:22. The intensive pattern, doubled sound, and distribution of the root all make coercion feel constitutive. As the first half of the closing pair, it rejects outward will imposed on others and prepares the final word’s rejection of inward refusal; the same paired certification returns in 19:32, while 11:59 gives an antithetical field where tyrant command and disobedience belong together.

topics.headline: negated tyrant class
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that Yahya is cleared from a whole overbearing identity class, not merely from a single behavior.
topics.reason: The word is the predicate of the negated copula and is indefinite accusative, supporting class-level exclusion.

topics.headline: forced repair becomes coercion
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices the concrete image of forced alignment behind the moral meaning of tyranny.
topics.reason: The repair branch is real root evidence, but local human predicate context narrows it to blameworthy coercion rather than legitimate restoration.

topics.headline: intensive form and doubled sound
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices coercion as a heavy, constitutive trait reinforced by form and sound.
topics.reason: The local form is tagged as an intensive adjective, and the shaddah and corpus distribution support the formal payoff.

topics.headline: wrong locus of compulsion
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the same root can be divine epithet at 59:23 or human vice in contexts such as 28:19 and 5:22, with authority and scope deciding the moral value.
topics.reason: The divine epithet contrast at 59:23 is valid, but local grammar applies the word to a human character under negation.

topics.headline: outward half of the rejected will-pair
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices the final profile as a paired rejection of coercing others and rebelling against rightful authority.
topics.reason: Attachment evidence binds the final adjective to this predicate, and inter-ayah rows show the same paired formula in 19:32 and an antithetical field in 11:59.

topics.headline: first half of heavy closure
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices the first final adjective setting up the sound and cadence of the denied vice pair.
topics.reason: The accusative ending and heavy consonantal cluster align with the following final adjective.

words.gloss_range: negated qualitative adjective for settled disobedient or rebellious character
words.root_gloss_range: disobedience, departure from obedience, resistance, and disputed staff-rigidity imagery; locally narrowed to settled moral refusal under negation

supporting_anchors.gloss_range: the preceding negated coercive predicate paired with the final refusal adjective

words.prose: {{ar:عَصِيًّۭا}} ({{tr:ʿaṣiyyā}}) closes the ayah as either a second predicate or a modifier within the same negated frame, so the final word denies a whole disobedient character type. Its qualitative form turns acts of refusal into a settled disposition, and the root’s relation to authority means the objectless adjective still implies refusal against rightful command. The disputed staff image can color that refusal as stiffness, but the local sense remains moral disobedience. In the closing pair, {{ar:جَبَّارًا}} ({{tr:jabbāran}}) names outward coercion and {{ar:عَصِيًّۭا}} ({{tr:ʿaṣiyyā}}) names inward refusal, so the ayah seals Yahya’s portrait by excluding both directions of distorted will. The same rare adjective and paired formula bind 19:14 to 19:32, while 19:44 later affirms disobedient being for Satan.

topics.headline: second denied trait under one negation
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that disobedience is denied as its own character type while remaining inside the same negated clause.
topics.reason: The final adjective agrees with the preceding predicate and can function as modifier or predicate mate; both readings stay under the same negation.

topics.headline: settled refusal quality
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the wording denies habitual rebellious disposition, not a single lapse.
topics.reason: The local form is a qualitative adjective, and the source rows contrast it with finite acts of disobedience.

topics.headline: rigidity image as color
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices disobedience with a felt stiffness, while keeping the local sense moral rather than concrete.
topics.reason: The staff-related dispute is valid as image pressure, but the local adjective and negated predicate frame select disobedience.

topics.headline: refusal implies authority relation
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that even without an explicit object, disobedience implies standing against rightful authority.
topics.reason: Distributional rows tie the root to God, messengers, and lordship, and nothing in the local clause supplies a different object.

topics.headline: final cadence seals exclusion
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the ayah ends on the excluded habit of rebellion, giving the negative verdict closure weight.
topics.reason: The word is final in the ayah, and the rows consistently treat its ending and pause position as closure force.

topics.headline: inward half of the rejected will-pair
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices the final pair as mirror vices: imposing will outward and refusing rightful will inward.
topics.reason: The final adjective is attached to the preceding predicate, and the CRITICAL rows provide concrete pair and contrast evidence including 11:59.

topics.headline: rare same-surah echo and Satan contrast
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the rare adjective binds Yahya’s negated profile to Isa’s in 19:32 and contrasts with Satan’s affirmed profile in 19:44.
topics.reason: The rows give concrete same-surah references and the contextual profile marks the form as low occurrence.

inter_ayah_rows.label: strong

inter_ayah_rows.label: weak
inter_ayah_rows.note: Disobedience to God and His messenger is only a general contrary boundary for عصي.

inter_ayah_rows.note: Divine incomparability has no bearing on filial goodness or arrogance.

inter_ayah_rows.label: strong
inter_ayah_rows.note: Yahya receives wisdom and firm responsibility immediately before his character is described.

inter_ayah_rows.label: weak
inter_ayah_rows.note: The righteous messengers share the root of goodness but add little beyond the focus's character term.

inter_ayah_rows.label: strong
inter_ayah_rows.note: Commands kindness to parents while setting a principled limit on obeying them in wrongdoing.

inter_ayah_rows.label: strong
inter_ayah_rows.note: Yahya's tenderness, purity, and piety directly precede and characterize the filial goodness in focus.

inter_ayah_rows.label: medium
inter_ayah_rows.note: The failure of every obstinate tyrant gives a clear contrary profile for not being jabbār.

inter_ayah_rows.label: medium
inter_ayah_rows.note: Links excellence toward parents with gratitude, maturity, and concern for one's offspring.

inter_ayah_rows.label: weak
inter_ayah_rows.note: Obedience after a settled divine command gives a broad contrast to being disobedient.

inter_ayah_rows.label: medium
inter_ayah_rows.note: Pharaoh's denial and disobedience form a concise contrary model to Yahya's non-rebellious character.

inter_ayah_rows.label: weak
inter_ayah_rows.note: God's lack of need for child or protector is a theological contrast, not a portrait of Yahya's family life.

inter_ayah_rows.label: medium
inter_ayah_rows.note: Continues the Zakariyya narrative that leads to the child whose character the focus records.

inter_ayah_rows.label: weak
inter_ayah_rows.note: A disputed charge of disobedience is too situational to add much to Yahya's trait.

inter_ayah_rows.label: no value
inter_ayah_rows.note: Intercessors and idolatry do not illuminate the focus.

inter_ayah_rows.label: strong
inter_ayah_rows.note: Zakariyya asks for an inheriting successor pleasing to God, directly framing Yahya's worthy filial character.

inter_ayah_rows.label: medium
inter_ayah_rows.note: Pairs arrogance and coercive power as a condemned character opposite to the focus's jabbār denial.

inter_ayah_rows.label: medium
inter_ayah_rows.note: Depicts tyrannical violence, sharpening the moral opposite of Yahya's non-jabbār disposition.

inter_ayah_rows.label: medium
inter_ayah_rows.note: Opens Zakariyya's story as divine mercy, the narrative source of Yahya's formation.

inter_ayah_rows.label: weak
inter_ayah_rows.note: God as al-Barr gives a broad divine-goodness resonance rather than a filial application.

inter_ayah_rows.label: medium
inter_ayah_rows.note: Contrasts reform with appearing as a coercive tyrant, clarifying the social force of jabbār.

inter_ayah_rows.label: medium
inter_ayah_rows.note: Models ethical separation from wrongdoing when others disobey, a secondary boundary for obedience.

inter_ayah_rows.label: weak
inter_ayah_rows.note: Disobedience and transgression bring condemnation, but the communal case is distant from the focus.

inter_ayah_rows.label: no value
inter_ayah_rows.note: God's unique creation and sovereignty do not clarify Yahya's conduct.

inter_ayah_rows.label: weak
inter_ayah_rows.note: Continues Zakariyya's sign, providing only narrative proximity before Yahya's birth.

inter_ayah_rows.label: medium
inter_ayah_rows.note: Fear of divine punishment for disobedience supplies a general contrary moral frame.

inter_ayah_rows.label: medium
inter_ayah_rows.note: Names Satan as disobedient while addressing a father, a secondary filial and contrary parallel.

inter_ayah_rows.label: strong
inter_ayah_rows.note: The announcement of Yahya directly identifies the child whose virtues are stated in the focus.

inter_ayah_rows.label: weak
inter_ayah_rows.note: Rejecting disobedience as contrary to right guidance is a broad ethical parallel.

inter_ayah_rows.label: no value
inter_ayah_rows.note: The legal procedure for spousal accusation is unrelated to filial righteousness.

inter_ayah_rows.label: strong
inter_ayah_rows.note: Zakariyya's astonishment at a son despite barrenness directly precedes Yahya's birth and character.

inter_ayah_rows.label: weak
inter_ayah_rows.note: The righteous share the root of goodness, but the verse concerns their reward rather than filial conduct.

inter_ayah_rows.label: medium
inter_ayah_rows.note: Following every obstinate tyrant combines the two contrary terms from the focus in a collective warning.

inter_ayah_rows.label: weak
inter_ayah_rows.note: A warning to a father about Satanic allegiance is a limited family-context contrast.

inter_ayah_rows.label: weak
inter_ayah_rows.note: The people's fear of tyrants offers only a distant contrast to Yahya not being jabbār.

inter_ayah_rows.label: medium
inter_ayah_rows.note: Late confession after sustained disobedience supplies a contrary trajectory to Yahya's obedience.

inter_ayah_rows.label: strong
inter_ayah_rows.note: Completes Yahya's immediate portrait with peace across birth, death, and resurrection.

inter_ayah_rows.label: weak
inter_ayah_rows.note: The people's declared disobedience is a broad contrary example with no filial connection.

inter_ayah_rows.label: weak
inter_ayah_rows.note: The righteous in bliss repeats the goodness root but is redundant after closer character parallels.

inter_ayah_rows.label: weak

inter_ayah_rows.label: weak

inter_ayah_rows.label: medium
inter_ayah_rows.note: Ishmael's care for his household and his pleasing standing offer a limited prophetic-family parallel.

inter_ayah_rows.label: medium

inter_ayah_rows.label: weak
inter_ayah_rows.note: Contrasts secret talk for goodness and piety with disobedience, but not in a family setting.

inter_ayah_rows.label: weak

inter_ayah_rows.label: weak

The womb is a bounded place of growth; the gift is prepared; birth opens into tenderness, purification, and reciprocal care. identity_judgment.rationale: Kaynak ifadesi koyunu sürerken veya yeme çağırırken çıkarılan sesi ve dille yapılan gürültülü, çok ya da yararsız konuşmayı destekler. lexicalization_scope.note: Koyuna yöneltilen ses ile çok ve gürültülü konuşma biçimleri, tartışmalı atasözü kullanımından ayrı tutulur.

concept_map.definition: Koyunu sürmek veya yeme çağırmak için çıkarılan ses ile dille yapılan gürültülü, çok, öfkeli ya da yararsız konuşmayı anlatır. Belirli bir atasözündeki anlamı ise kaynaklara göre değişir ve çekirdeğe genellenemez.

facets.statement: Sürülen veya yeme çağrılan koyuna yöneltilen ses.
Dille çıkarılan gürültü ve özellikle öfkeli, çok ya da yararsız konuşma.

Buğdayın tek bir tanesi.

Toprağın bol miktarda buğday vermesi.

identity_judgment.rationale: Kaynak ifadesi bir şeyin başka bir şeyden bir nedenle ortaya çıkmasını çekirdek yapar; sonradan oluşturulmuş söz, uydurulmuş kitap veya kanıt ve katışıksız sayılmayan dil ya da kişi kullanımlarını buna bağlar. Verilen dal bu çekirdek ile uzantıları doğru biçimde toplar.

Sonradan oluşturulan söz bu ortaya çıkma düşüncesinin bir uzantısıdır.

concept_map.definition: Bir kişiyi istemediği bir işi yapmaya güç ve baskıyla yöneltmek, onun seçimini etkisiz bırakmaktır. Bu çekirdek, zorla egemen olan veya haksız yere öldüren kişi nitelemesine ve insan eylemlerini zorunlu sayan öğretiye genişler.

facets.statement: Bir kişi istemediği bir işi yapmaya güç veya baskıyla zorlanır.

Haksız yere öldüren ve yönetimi altındakilere zorbalık eden kişi bu nitelemeyle anılır.
Bir öğreti, insan eylemlerinin özgür seçimle değil zorunlu olarak gerçekleştiğini savunur.

identity_judgment.rationale: Kaynak deyişinin ortak çekirdeği, bir kimsenin kendisine buyruk verenin sözünü tutmaması ve ondan beklenen boyun eğme çizgisinden çıkmasıdır. Sağlanan dal çerçevesi bunu doğru yansıtır; bir topluluğun yöneticisinin sözünden çıkması bu çekirdeğin özel bir görünümüdür.
